**Visual observations:**
- Central foreground plant is notably shorter/more stunted than surrounding corn plants at the same growth stage
- The stunted plant shows lighter, yellowish-green coloration compared to the healthy dark green neighbors
- No visible leaf spots, lesions, rust pustules, tar spots, or smut galls
- Leaf shape appears relatively normal (no mosaic streaking or severe distortion)
- Whole-plant stunting is the dominant symptom

**Reasoning:**
The key feature here is a single plant that is significantly stunted relative to its neighbors, with mild chlorosis (lighter green). No spot/lesion diseases (Gray leaf spot, Northern corn leaf blight, Tar spot, etc.) fit because there are no lesions. No ear symptoms are visible. Mosaic viruses typically show clear streaking/mosaic patterns on leaves, which are not prominent here. Crazy top would show proliferating leafy growth at the top. Corn Stunt Spiroplasma is the classic cause of severe whole-plant stunting with chlorosis in corn, matching this image best.
